text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Chancellor Kohl's Christian Democrats and opposition Social Democrats renew attempt to hold talks on tax reform
- Self-employed say government tax reform plans do not go far enough
- Dutch foreign minister praises fruitful EU meeting in Noordwijk; no concrete results
- Demand for German environmental technology declines
- Employers' association says no chance of halving unemployment by 2000
HANDELSBLATT
- Tax talks between government and opposition to resume
- Finance Minister Waigel insists Maastricht criteria for monetary union will be interpreted strictly
- Commerzbank pre-tax profit rises 50 percent
- Dollar leaps to 1.71 billion marks
- Institutions say foreign takeovers of German firms will be much more common in future
- Foreign Ministers' meeting makes little progress on EU reform
- Industrial electricity users expect price cuts of 10 percent after liberalisation of power market
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Kohl ready to meet SPD leader Lafontaine in tax talks
- CDU leadership unanimously nominates Kohl to run for chancellor in next election
- Municipalities oppose use of detectives to combat welfare abuse
- Small and medium-sized German companies failing to keep up in use of Internet
- Utility firm RWE against payment of tax on reserves
- Cabinet puts off discussion of bill to limit power of banks
DIE WELT
- Tax talks between government and opposition to resume
- Row over institutions holds up EU reform
- Japanese Emperor praises Germany's efforts at European integration
- Employers and unions say little chance of halving unemployment by 2000
- Waigel and Bundesbank president Tietmeyer stick to strict interpretation of EMU criteria
- Growth prospects improve as all sectors report above-average expectations
-- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097160
